documents.title: Question about getting pregnant
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, it's been over a year now that we've been trying and nothing yet. My periods are still regular. You mentioned last summer to check in if it got to a year. Should I come in or go straight to a gynecologist?

documents.title: RE: Question about getting pregnant
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Nicole, the doctor would like to see you first to go over things and send the referral. We have June 11 at 3:30 open, does that work? Reply here and we'll lock it in.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28 y/o here because she and her husband have not conceived after about 13 months of regular unprotected intercourse.

Cycles regular, every 28-30 days, flow normal. No bleeding between periods. Never had a sexually transmitted infection, never had pelvic or abdominal surgery, has never been told she has endometriosis. No galactorrhea, no change in hair or skin, no heat or cold intolerance. Weight stable. Husband has not had any testing yet.

Meds: none. Allergies: none to medications.

Exam: BP and pulse as charted, weight unchanged from last year. Thyroid normal size, no nodules. No hirsutism or acne. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P: Infertility, >12 months, regular cycles, no obvious risk factors. Discussed that the workup involves both partners. Referral to Ob/Gyn for evaluation; they will likely coordinate hormone testing around her cycle, imaging, and a semen analysis for her husband, so I am not duplicating labs here. She is comfortable with that plan.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily on cycle days 5 through 9

reports.text: Transvaginal technique. Uterus anteverted, normal in size and contour, homogeneous myometrium. Endometrium thin and uniform, appropriate for early follicular phase. Right and left ovaries normal in size, each with several small antral follicles. No adnexal mass. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Normal uterus and ovaries; small antral follicles bilaterally.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP - CONSULTATION LETTER
Visit date: 07/16/2024
Reason for referral: infertility

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Rousseau, a 28-year-old nulligravida. She and her partner have had 14 months of unprotected intercourse without a pregnancy. Menses every 28 to 30 days. No STI history, no prior pelvic surgery and no known endometriosis.

Medications: none. Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: maternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes; mother hypothyroid; father hypertensive. No relatives with infertility, endometriosis or early menopause.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, works as a high school math teacher.

Examination: normal general, breast, abdominal and pelvic exam.

Data: Day-3 bloodwork drawn here last week shows normal TSH, prolactin, FSH and LH. Her partner's semen analysis was normal. Transvaginal ultrasound in our office today: normal uterus, both ovaries normal with small antral follicles.

Impression: female infertility, unexplained on the evaluation so far. Tubal patency still needs to be confirmed.

Plan: hysterosalpingogram scheduled for the next follicular window. Assuming the tubes are open, she will start clomiphene citrate 50 mg on cycle days 5-9 to promote ovulation, with timed intercourse. Prescription sent. Follow-up in about two months.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Consult letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gyn consult reviewed. Infertility added to problem list. Clomiphene cycles planned after HSG. Will let gyn manage.

reports.text: Indication: infertility. Cycle day 8, negative pregnancy test confirmed by the ordering office. After sterile preparation the cervix was cannulated and water-soluble contrast instilled under fluoroscopy. The uterine cavity is normal in size and shape with smooth margins and no filling defect. Both fallopian tubes fill promptly along their full length with free intraperitoneal spill bilaterally. No complications.

documents.title: Hysterosalpingogram
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Copy of outside HSG report received from the gynecology office. Normal uterine cavity, both tubes patent with free spill. Filed.

conditions.label: Dysmenorrhea
conditions.note: mild cramps with menses, no treatment

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (100 mg) by mouth daily on cycle days 5 through 9 for the challenge test

documents.title: Gynecology follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Visit date: 09/17/2024

Ms. Rousseau came back to review her fertility evaluation and to plan ovarian reserve testing. Per her intake the couple has been trying for 14 months. Cycles remain regular at about 29 days. She gets mild cramping with her periods; no abnormal bleeding and no pelvic pain otherwise. She completed two cycles of clomiphene 50 mg since July without conceiving.

Allergies: NKDA. She does not smoke or drink; BMI in the healthy range.
Exam today unremarkable.

Results to date: baseline TSH, prolactin, FSH, LH and estradiol all normal. HSG 07/29: normal cavity, both tubes patent. Husband's semen analysis within normal limits.

Assessment:
1. Unexplained infertility.
2. Dysmenorrhea, mild, not needing treatment.
3. Indication for clomiphene citrate challenge testing to assess ovarian reserve.

Plan: clomiphene citrate challenge test with her next cycle. Day-3 FSH and estradiol, clomiphene 100 mg on days 5 through 9, then day-10 FSH. We will send results and discuss next steps.

documents.title: Follow-up letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gyn f/u letter reviewed. HSG normal, unexplained infertility. Mild dysmenorrhea added. Challenge test next cycle. Problem list updated.

documents.title: Gynecology results letter
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP - RESULTS

Clomiphene citrate challenge test, October 2024:
- Cycle day 3 (10/07): FSH 6.8 IU/L, estradiol 38 pg/mL
- Cycle day 10 (10/14), after clomiphene 100 mg days 5-9: FSH 7.4 IU/L

Interpretation: normal response; no evidence of diminished ovarian reserve.

I reviewed these with Ms. Rousseau by phone. We talked about further clomiphene ovulation-induction cycles. She would like to wait for now and will call our office when she is ready to resume. No medications at this time. NKDA.

documents.title: Results letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Challenge test normal. Pausing treatment by her choice, gyn to resume when she calls. Testing item closed on problem list.
